_note: GENAI PRESETS - the second preset list.
Kept in its own file, not in styles.json, so the original preset list is
untouched and the two can be switched between in the GUI (Classic / GENAI
Presets). write_story.js searches this file after styles.json, so a preset id
works the same wherever it lives.
These are ported from the creator's 'master prompt' documents. Each document
has two halves: a set of reference IMAGE prompts (the look) and a SCRIPT
formula (the narrative engine). A preset is the two carried together:
style / whisk / cast_idiom / palette / camera  <- the reference prompts
direction / story_shapes / narration_voice      <- the script formula
Same rules as styles.json: `style` and `whisk` must never name a real studio,
channel or anime title; the words describe the look instead.

Then: family background and early hardship; early signs of talent with one specific anecdote; at least one vivid ORIGIN MOMENT told as a mini-scene rather than stated as fact; a chronological career arc through struggle, breakthrough, recognition, peak, controversy and legacy; one central 'miracle period' framed as the turning point; personal life woven through, flaws included, so the subject is not one-dimensional; the larger historical forces of their time; what their work still means for ordinary people today; any real contradiction or moral complexity honestly; later years and death factually; and a closing legacy that ends on one or two open questions to the audience. One narrator, no on-screen text.

Close on one short ironic line that ties back to the opening exhibit. Use phones, cameras and records as a recurring motif. One narrator, no on-screen text.

styles.direction: A health EXPLAINER that myth-busts, not a lecture. Clip 1 is a HOOK that contradicts a widely-held belief in one or two punchy sentences and immediately gives the single most surprising real statistic. Then split the audience into four to six bands they can self-identify with, ordered to the rarest last. For each band: address the viewer directly ('if this is you'), give ONE genuine science-backed advantage with a number, make the mechanism intuitive with a plain everyday metaphor, pivot on a 'but' to ONE genuine cost for that same group, close the band on a short quotable one-liner, and slide into the next band. Past halfway, drop a real scientific twist that complicates the pattern, then anchor it on one concrete human case, and close by saying no group wins outright - daily choices matter more than the trait. End on a question the viewer can answer about themselves. One narrator, no on-screen text.

styles.direction: A personal-finance EXPLAINER that busts a myth, in a handcrafted paper-diorama style. Clip 1 is a HOOK that opens on a frustration about a common money mistake, made absurd and visual with a physical analogy like a leaking bucket. Then introduce the host briefly, drop one surprising sourced statistic, and promise a specific CORRECT ORDER that most people skip. Explain why order beats enthusiasm with a house-foundation metaphor, then walk the numbered sequence: each step states the step, why it comes here, one concrete number or dollar example, one memorable analogy, one counterintuitive nuance, and a mini-payoff. Reinforce with one more statistic past halfway, reward the viewer for making it this far, recap the whole order in one tight sentence, and close looking forward to their future self. Every number must be concrete and translated into something a person can picture. One narrator, no on-screen text.

styles.direction: A finance and economics DOCUMENTARY, calm but building to a reveal. Clip 1 is a COLD OPEN of three to five rapid rhetorical questions most people have never had answered, framing the subject as a hidden mechanism with massive invisible power, plus one striking claim that sounds unbelievable but is true. Then explain the real mechanics plainly with an everyday analogy and debunk one common misconception about how the system works; trace its origin through two to four turning points with short connecting lines; name clearly who benefits and who pays, with one callous-sounding insider line; zoom out to the systemic stakes and a past crisis as a cautionary parallel; present one or two genuine reform ideas attributed to real thinkers, acknowledging the political difficulty honestly; and close on one line that reframes the whole topic. styles.direction: A space DOCUMENTARY that runs on awe. Clip 1 is a COLD OPEN on the single most mind-blowing moment or discovery in the story, described vividly and without its full context, to hook before rewinding. Then the middle runs as chronological problem-breakthrough-surprise episodes: the limitation or assumption of the time, who challenged it and how - a person, an instrument, an accident - what surprising thing came out of it, and how it reshaped what followed. Use real named people, dates and concrete physical detail. Weave in two or three moments of real personal risk, failure or controversy. Climb a ladder of escalating numbers so the scale keeps growing, describe each instrument or method as a physical, almost magic machine rather than as a spec sheet, and close on what is still unknown. One narrator, no on-screen text.
